name: Yala National Park
tagline: One of the best places in the world to see wild leopards, plus elephants, sloth bears, crocodiles and hundreds of birds in dry scrub and lagoon country.
highlight: A leopard stretched along a rock in early morning light, watched from the safety of a jeep.
shortDescription: Sri Lanka's most famous safari park, with one of the highest densities of leopards in the world, elephants, buffalo, crocodiles and birds, explored in jeep safaris.
metaDescription: A Yala National Park travel guide: leopard safaris, elephants, jeep tours and tickets, best time, blocks, Udawalawe alternative, where to stay, how to get there and a two-day plan.

intro: Yala National Park in south-eastern Sri Lanka covers almost 1,000 square kilometres of scrub, forest, rocky outcrops and lagoons along the Indian Ocean. It is the country's most visited park and one of the world's best places to see wild leopards, the Sri Lankan subspecies, with a density among the highest recorded. The park is divided into blocks, and the accessible Block 1 draws the most safari jeeps.

Leopards are the main quarry, but the park also has Asian elephants, water buffalo, sloth bears, crocodiles, jackals, mongoose and more than 200 bird species, including peacocks, painted storks and eagles. Tours run at dawn and in the afternoon, in open jeeps with local trackers, and take three to four hours. Sightings are never guaranteed, though leopards are seen on many drives.

Yala can be busy, with many jeeps converging on a single sighting, so choose an operator that behaves responsibly and consider quieter parks such as Udawalawe for elephants, or Wilpattu in the north-west for leopards. Yala is about five to six hours from Colombo, so it is often combined with Ella and the south coast.
